# XAS Step Planner

Use this skill when the user request is not just "run the whole workflow", but may ask for a subset of XAS processing steps.

This skill defines a fixed step catalog, a plan-first execution pattern, and rules for mapping user requests onto steps.

## Goal

Support both:
- Full workflow requests such as "do the first-shell fit" or "match this spectrum"
- Partial requests such as "just preprocess the data", "show the preprocessing plots", "only detect the element", or "only manipulate the data"

The agent should:
1. Read the user request
2. Produce a short structured plan using steps from the catalog below
3. Execute only the required steps
4. Reuse prior artifacts when possible instead of recomputing

## Design Rules

- Keep the step catalog fixed. The agent may choose steps, but should not invent new step names at runtime.
- Separate library functions from tool wrappers.
- Prefer step outputs that can be passed to later steps by stable artifact ids.
- Keep "full workflow" tools as convenience wrappers, but implement them by calling the same step library.
- If a requested step is not implemented yet, say that clearly and fall back to the closest available workflow.

## Artifact Types

Use stable references between steps instead of passing large raw objects through the agent.

- `xas_ref`: loaded and preprocessed spectrum artifact
- `paths_ref`: FEFF path preparation artifact
- `fit_ref`: fit execution artifact
- `match_ref`: spectra matching artifact
- `plot_ref`: saved plot artifact or JSON plot payload reference
- `multi_report_ref`: grouped multi-spectrum preview/report payload

## Step Catalog

### Shared Data Steps

#### `prepare_multi_spectrum_reports`

Purpose:
- Prepare grouped right-panel reports for several spectra in one request
- Keep one report per spectrum so the frontend can switch between them

Inputs:
- list of `xas_path` values for the spectra that should be reviewed together

Outputs:
- `multi_report_ref`
- one preview group per spectrum, each with its own plots and report metadata

Use this when:
- the user asks to compare multiple spectra
- the user asks to plot/show/analyze several attached spectra together
- the user refers to "both", "all", "multiple", or more than one uploaded spectrum in a single visualization-style request

Do not use this when:
- the user clearly refers to only one specific spectrum
- the task is a single-spectrum fit or single-spectrum database match

#### `prepare_multi_fit_reports`

Purpose:
- Run first-shell fitting for several spectra against one shared CIF/structure
- Return one right-panel report per fitted spectrum so the frontend can switch between them

Inputs:
- one `material_id` or equivalent resolved structure context
- list of `xas_path` values for the spectra to fit together
- optional fit parameter overrides

Outputs:
- `multi_report_ref`
- one preview group per spectrum, each with its own fit summary, tables, and chi-fit plots

Use this when:
- the user asks to fit both/all/multiple attached spectra with the same CIF
- the user asks for parallel multi-spectrum fitting
- one structure is shared across multiple uploaded spectra

Do not use this when:
- the user asked to fit only one specific spectrum
- the task is only plotting/preprocessing without fitting

#### `load_and_preprocess_xas`

Purpose:
- Load raw XAS input
- Parse energy and mu-like signals
- Run normalization and standard preprocessing

Inputs:
- `xas_path`

Outputs:
- `xas_ref`
- optional summary fields such as `e0`, data length, detected columns, file type

Maps to current code:
- `load_prj_first_shell()` in `backend/function_calling/xas_io.py`
- `load_user_spectrum()` in `backend/function_calling/spectra_matching.py`

#### `calibrate_xas_energy`

Purpose:
- Apply optional foil-based energy calibration before fitting or plotting
- Shift the sample energy axis by the foil-derived offset

Inputs:
- `xas_path` or `xas_ref` for the sample
- `foil_xas_path` or `foil_xas_ref` for the foil reference
- optional accepted foil edge energy or foil element/edge metadata

Outputs:
- calibrated `xas_ref`
- calibration metadata such as measured foil edge, accepted foil edge, and applied energy offset

Use this when:
- the user explicitly asks for energy calibration
- the user explicitly mentions foil calibration, foil data, foil reference, or energy offset correction
- the user asks to calibrate first and then fit

Do not use this when:
- the user did not ask for calibration
- no foil reference is available and the user only asked for a normal fit

Planning rule:
- Treat foil calibration as opt-in.
- If the uploaded spectrum itself is a foil/reference scan and the user explicitly asks for calibration, allow calibration from that spectrum alone by aligning its derivative edge position to the accepted reference edge energy.
- Only use that self-calibration path when the user explicitly identifies the current uploaded spectrum as the foil/reference scan. Do not treat a normal sample scan as a foil based only on element or edge matching.
- If self-calibration is allowed and the foil element was not provided, use `detect_xas_element` first to infer the likely foil element from the edge-detection result before asking the user.
- After `detect_xas_element` returns a likely foil element, use that inferred element to attempt calibration and let the calibration step resolve the accepted reference energy when possible.
- Only ask the user for foil element, edge, or accepted edge energy if edge-based inference still does not give enough information to complete calibration reliably.
- If the user asks for calibration, first check whether the uploaded scan already contains embedded foil/reference channels such as `It` and `Iref`.
- If the scan is not itself the foil/reference and embedded foil/reference channels are present, use them automatically before asking for a separate foil file.
- If no embedded foil/reference scan is available, then check for a separate foil/reference file in the current context.
- If neither embedded nor separate foil/reference data is available, ask the user to provide foil data.
- Do not block ordinary fitting or preprocessing on foil calibration unless the user explicitly requested calibration.
- If calibration already produced a calibrated `xas_ref` earlier in the conversation, reuse that calibrated artifact for later fitting or plotting requests instead of asking for foil data again.

#### `manipulate_xas_data`

Purpose:
- Apply user-requested data changes before fitting or matching

Typical operations:
- crop energy range
- smooth signal
- regrid or interpolate
- baseline correction
- rename columns or select signal source

Inputs:
- `xas_ref`
- manipulation parameters

Outputs:
- updated `xas_ref`

Use only when the user explicitly asks for data manipulation or when a workflow requires a deterministic normalization/cropping step.

#### `plot_preprocessed_xas`

Purpose:
- Show preprocessing results without running fitting or matching

Inputs:
- `xas_ref`

Outputs:
- `plot_ref`

Typical plots:
- raw mu
- normalized mu
- chi(k)
- chi(R), if available from preprocessing

### First-Shell Fitting Steps

#### `prepare_feff_paths`

Purpose:
- Generate and select FEFF paths for fitting

Inputs:
- `material_id`
- optional `edge`
- optional `radius`
- optional path filters such as `amp_ratio` and `r_max`

Outputs:
- `paths_ref`
- path summary

Maps to current code:
- `make_and_run_feff()` and `load_paths()` in `backend/function_calling/feff.py`

#### `build_first_shell_fit_inputs`

Purpose:
- Assemble fit parameters, selected path list, and transform settings for first-shell fitting

Inputs:
- `xas_ref`
- `paths_ref`
- fit parameters such as `amp`, `e0`, `sigma2`, `deltar`
- optional transform settings
- optional prior calibration metadata when foil calibration was requested

Outputs:
- prepared fit input bundle or normalized arguments for the fit step

This step exists to keep parameter setup separate from long-running fit execution.

#### `execute_first_shell_fit`

Purpose:
- Execute the fit

Inputs:
- prepared fit inputs, or `xas_ref` + `paths_ref` + fit params

Outputs:
- `fit_ref`
- lightweight status fields such as reduced chi-squared and r-factor

Maps to current code:
- `feffpath()`, `feffit_transform()`, `feffit_dataset()`, `feffit()` flow wired through `backend/function_calling/tools.py` and `backend/function_calling/fit.py`

This should be the only long-running fitting step.

#### `extract_first_shell_fit_results`

Purpose:
- Extract fit summary and path parameters from `fit_ref`

Inputs:
- `fit_ref`

Outputs:
- fit result JSON

Maps to current code:
- `extract_fitted_parameters()` and `extract_path_parameters()` in `backend/function_calling/fit.py`

#### `plot_first_shell_fit`

Purpose:
- Generate fit plots without rerunning the fit

Inputs:
- `fit_ref`

Outputs:
- `plot_ref`

Maps to current code:
- `viz_first_shell()` in `backend/function_calling/reports.py`

Do not recompute the fit here. Consume saved fit artifacts.

### Spectra Matching Steps

#### `detect_xas_element`

Purpose:
- Identify the absorbing element before matching
- Help infer the likely foil element from edge detection when a foil scan needs self-calibration

Inputs:
- `xas_ref`

Outputs:
- detected `element`
- optional `e0`

Maps to current code:
- `EdgeIdentifier` usage in `backend/function_calling/tools.py`

#### `fetch_reference_spectra`

Purpose:
- Load candidate reference spectra for a known element

Inputs:
- `element`

Outputs:
- reference spectra set or internal reference handle

Maps to current code:
- `get_normalized_db_spectra()` in `backend/function_calling/spectra_matching.py`

#### `match_reference_spectra`

Purpose:
- Score the user spectrum against the reference set

Inputs:
- `xas_ref`
- `element` or reference handle
- optional `top_n`

Outputs:
- `match_ref`
- top matches

Maps to current code:
- `match_spectra()` in `backend/function_calling/spectra_matching.py`

#### `plot_reference_matches`

Purpose:
- Plot top matches without rerunning the match logic

Inputs:
- `match_ref`

Outputs:
- `plot_ref`

Maps to current code:
- `plot_matches()` in `backend/function_calling/reports.py`

## Full Workflow Wrappers

These are convenience tools for simple user requests.

### `orchestrate_first_shell_fit`

Execute:
1. `prepare_feff_paths`
2. `load_and_preprocess_xas`
3. `build_first_shell_fit_inputs`
4. `execute_first_shell_fit`
5. `extract_first_shell_fit_results`
6. `plot_first_shell_fit`

### `run_spectrum_match_workflow`

Execute:
1. `load_and_preprocess_xas`
2. `detect_xas_element` if element not provided
3. `fetch_reference_spectra`
4. `match_reference_spectra`
5. `plot_reference_matches` if plots are requested

## Planning Rules

Use the smallest valid plan that satisfies the request.

Examples:

- "Do first-shell fitting"
  - Use the full fitting workflow

- "Just show the preprocessing plots"
  - `load_and_preprocess_xas`
  - `plot_preprocessed_xas`

- "Only detect the element and match it"
  - `load_and_preprocess_xas`
  - `detect_xas_element`
  - `fetch_reference_spectra`
  - `match_reference_spectra`

- "Crop the data to a smaller range and then fit"
  - `load_and_preprocess_xas`
  - `manipulate_xas_data`
  - `prepare_feff_paths`
  - `build_first_shell_fit_inputs`
  - `execute_first_shell_fit`
  - `extract_first_shell_fit_results`

- "Plot the fit again"
  - `plot_first_shell_fit`
  - Reuse existing `fit_ref`

## Plan Format

Prefer a short JSON-like plan before execution:

```json
{
  "goal": "show preprocessing plots",
  "steps": [
    {"step": "load_and_preprocess_xas", "args": {"xas_path": "<path>"}},
    {"step": "plot_preprocessed_xas", "args": {"xas_ref": "<from previous step>"}}
  ]
}
```

Keep the plan short. Do not include internal reasoning.

## Execution Rules

- Reuse artifacts when they already exist and are still valid.
- Do not rerun FEFF generation or fitting if the request only needs plotting or extraction.
- Do not hide multi-step work inside a tool if the user asked for only one step.
- Return step-level outputs in a form that downstream steps can reuse.
- If plotting is optional, skip it unless the user requested it or the workflow requires it.
- Do not show the internal plan JSON to the user.
- Do not return raw local filesystem paths in the user-facing answer.
- Summarize outputs naturally for chat, and rely on structured preview metadata for plots and reports.

# Database Access Workflow

Use this skill when the user wants the agent to fetch a structure or a spectrum from the project-connected databases instead of uploading files manually.

## Available tools

- `lookup_material_structure(query)`
  Resolve a formula like `CoO` or a Materials Project id like `mp-19009` into a local CIF path plus the resolved material id.
- `search_xafs_database(query, limit=10)`
  Search the MDR/NIMS XAFS catalog by material name, specimen text, title, or dataset id.
- `fetch_xafs_dataset(dataset_id)`
  Download the selected dataset and return local file paths plus `primary_path`, which is the best default spectrum file to use next.

## When to use which tool

- If the user asks for a CIF, structure, Materials Project lookup, or "material database" lookup, start with `lookup_material_structure`.
- If the user asks for an online XAS spectrum, MDR dataset, NIMS dataset, or "spectrum database" lookup, start with `search_xafs_database`.
- If `search_xafs_database` returns one clearly correct match, fetch it directly.
- If it returns several plausible matches and the right one is not obvious, ask the user a short disambiguating question.

## How to continue after retrieval

- After `lookup_material_structure`, use the returned `material_id` as the structure context for FEFF-path or fitting work.
- After `fetch_xafs_dataset`, use `primary_path` as the default input to:

`ask_xas_literature` (synthesized, `[n]`-cited answer) and `search_xas_literature`
(raw cited hits) tools. Retrieval is **hybrid** — exact-term lexical search fused with
semantic search — and degrades gracefully if optional deps are missing.

**Layer 1 — Dr.XAS tool-parameter reference (114 cards across 30 of
your own analysis tools).** Authoritative parameters, defaults, and meanings of the
tools you yourself run — e.g. `rbkg` (default 1.0) and `kweight` (default 2) in
`remove_xas_background`, `nnorm`/`nvict` in `normalize_xas_data`, k/R ranges in the
EXAFS fits. Use these for "what value should I use for X", "what is the default of Y",
or "what does parameter Z do". Pass `source='drxas_tool'` to restrict to this layer.
These cards describe the *tools*; to actually process the user's spectrum, call the
analysis tool itself.

tools.name: check_xas_data_quality
tools.description:
Assess the data quality of an XAS spectrum and return a graded report.

Runs the standard larch preprocessing (`pre_edge`, `autobk`) on the
spectrum and evaluates a set of physically grounded quality metrics:
grid integrity (finite values, a strictly increasing energy axis, point
density, sampling uniformity), edge quality (edge step and the energy
range available below/above E0 for normalization), and noise (a
normalized-μ signal-to-noise estimate from the flat pre-edge region plus
the χ(k) noise level and usable k-range from `larch.xafs.estimate_noise`).

Returns per-check verdicts (ok / warning / fail), an overall grade
(excellent / good / fair / poor) with a 0–100 score, the key metrics, and
actionable recommendations. Reads the processed spectrum and returns a
diagnostic only; it does NOT write a new spectrum artifact or change the
active `xas_ref`. `current_transform` reports the saved FT settings so changes
to one limit can preserve the others; an empty object means no saved settings.

tools.name: normalize_xas_data
tools.description:
Re-run edge-step normalization on an XAS spectrum with explicit control
over the larch `pre_edge` parameters, and write the normalized result as a
new reusable processed-spectrum artifact.

The standard load pipeline normalizes with default parameters; use this
tool when that normalization is wrong or needs tuning (e.g. the edge step,
pre-edge slope, or post-edge flattening look off).

Leaving a parameter unset lets larch choose it. The returned report echoes
the parameters that were actually applied. Reuse the returned `xas_ref`
for later plotting, matching, calibration, or fitting.

pre1.description: pre-edge line fit range in eV relative to E0 (negative).
pre1.title: Pre1

pre2.description: pre-edge line fit range in eV relative to E0 (negative).
pre2.title: Pre2

norm1.description: normalization range in eV relative to E0 (positive).
norm1.title: Norm1

norm2.description: normalization range in eV relative to E0 (positive).
norm2.title: Norm2

nnorm.description: degree of the post-edge normalization polynomial (0–3).
nnorm.title: Nnorm

nvict.description: Victoreen order for the pre-edge fit (default 0).
nvict.title: Nvict

tools.name: remove_xas_background
tools.description:
Re-run the Autobk EXAFS background subtraction on an XAS spectrum with
explicit control over the larch `autobk` parameters, and write the result
as a new reusable processed-spectrum artifact.

The standard load pipeline removes the background with fixed
`rbkg=1.0, kweight=2`; use this tool when the extracted χ(k) shows
low-R leakage, over/under-subtraction, or needs tuning.

Leaving a parameter unset lets larch choose it. The returned report echoes
the parameters that were actually applied. Reuse the returned `xas_ref`
for later plotting, matching, calibration, or fitting.

tools.name: align_xas_spectra
tools.description:
Align a spectrum to a reference by the energy shift that best matches their
derivative spectra around the edge, and write the aligned spectrum as a new
reusable artifact.

Use this to put two sample spectra on a common energy axis (e.g. before
merging or linear-combination fitting) when scans are offset in energy. This
is a relative alignment, distinct from absolute foil-based
`calibrate_xas_energy`. Provide the reference via `reference_xas_ref`/
`reference_xas_path`. Reuse the returned `xas_ref`.

max_shift.description:
how far, in eV, the derivative-matching refinement may move
away from the initial edge-to-edge guess (the steepest-slope point of
each spectrum). It does not cap the applied shift, which can exceed
it when the edges are far apart; a glitch at the steepest slope can
mislead that guess, so check `energy_shift_ev` against
`target_edge_before_ev` and `reference_edge_ev`.
max_shift.title: Max Shift

emin.description:
lower bound, in absolute eV on the reference energy axis, of the
derivative-matching window. Pass it (with `emax`) whenever the user
names a comparison range; omitted, the window is 40 eV centered on
the reference edge.
emin.title: Emin

emax.description: upper bound, in absolute eV, of the derivative-matching window.
emax.title: Emax

tools.name: merge_xas_spectra
tools.description:
Merge/average several repeat XAS scans into one higher-SNR spectrum and
write it as a new reusable processed-spectrum artifact.

Each input scan's μ(E) is interpolated onto a common energy grid (via
larch.io.merge_groups) and averaged; averaging N independent scans reduces
the noise amplitude by roughly √N. Use this when the user has multiple
repeat scans of the same sample, or when the data-quality check flags low
signal-to-noise and repeats are available.

Provide at least two spectra via `xas_refs` (already-processed artifacts)
and/or `xas_paths` (raw files). `kind` is the interpolation kind and `trim`
keeps only the overlapping energy range. Reuse the returned `xas_ref` for
later plotting, matching, calibration, or fitting.

tools.name: fourier_transform_xas
tools.description:
Fourier transform χ(k) → χ(R) with a tunable k-window, k-weighting, and window
shape, and write a new processed χ(R) artifact plus the R-space figures.

Omitted or null parameters preserve the source artifact's saved FT settings.
Pass null for every setting the user did not ask to change. For example, an
upper-limit-only change supplies kmax and leaves kmin/dk/kweight/window/rmax_out
null. Explicit values override saved settings, including an explicit kmin=0.
If no setting was saved, defaults are kmin=2, full available kmax, dk=1,
kweight=2, window=kaiser, rmax_out=10. The quality tool reports current_transform.

Also returns ``n_independent`` (Nyquist ``2·Δk·ΔR/π + 2``) as an
over-parameterization guardrail for later fitting.

kmin.description: Lower k bound in Å⁻¹; null preserves the current lower limit.
kmin.title: Kmin

kmax.description: Upper k bound in Å⁻¹; null preserves the current upper limit.
kmax.title: Kmax

rmax_out.description: highest R (Å) in the output χ(R).
rmax_out.title: Rmax Out

tools.name: assess_shell_structure
tools.description:
Assess coordination-shell structure from |χ(R)| and recommend a fit scope
(first-shell vs. multishell) — decision support, not a fit.

Counts the resolved peaks in the Fourier-transform magnitude |χ(R)|, weighs
them against the information budget the available k-range affords (Nyquist
independent points), and returns a `first_shell`/`multishell` recommendation
with explicit reasons, the peak list (χ(R)-space positions, phase-shifted
below true distances), the FT resolution, and the first-shell/multishell
independent-point counts. Reads the processed spectrum and returns a
diagnostic; it does NOT run a fit or change the active `xas_ref`. Use it
before deciding between a first-shell and a multishell fit, or when the user
asks how many shells are present or which fit is appropriate.

tools.name: fit_ffef_first_shell
tools.description:
`absorber` selects a chemical element in the CIF. Fits infer it only from a
    unique measured-edge match; otherwise specify it explicitly. `edge` is the
    measured edge family (K, L1, L2, L3; L means L3). Inconsistent spectra/CIFs fail.
    Fit XAFS data using the provided parameters to FEFF paths.
    This is the default workflow for a single first-shell fit.
    Prefer `robust_first_shell_fit` instead when the user wants a
    careful/robust/publication-quality fit or asks how trustworthy a fit is.

    Leave `kmin`, `kmax`, `rmin`, and `rmax` unset/null to automatically select
    first-shell k/R bounds from noise, Fourier peaks, and candidate fits. Any
    explicit boundary preserves manual control, filling other omitted boundaries
    with k 3–10 Å⁻¹ and R 1–3 Å. `auto_select_window=True` explicitly selects all
    four bounds; False disables selection. Automatic selection retains the current
    preprocessing, constraints, kweight (default 2) and dk (default 4, Kaiser).
    Its phase-uncorrected R window can include multiple shells; inspect the returned
    `window_selection` diagnostics. This does not apply theory-guided Autobk.
    Set `fix_s02=True` to hold S0² fixed at the provided `params.amp` (transfer it
    from a reference standard to break the S0²/σ² degeneracy). Prefer tuning the
    window when the data quality or shell structure calls for it (e.g. a shorter
    `kmax` for noisy data), rather than leaving the defaults blindly.

    Canonical fit-parameter names for first-shell: `amp` (S0²), `e0` (ΔE0),
    `sigma2` (Debye-Waller σ²), `deltar` (bond-length shift ΔR).

    `constraints` (optional) fixes, bounds, or links fit parameters for
    publication-grade control: each entry names one of the four canonical
    parameters above and may set `vary` (False to fix, e.g. hold S0² from a
    standard), `min`/`max`, `value`, or `expr` (a larch link expression such
    as `"alpha"` to tie ΔR to a user-defined symbol).

    `defs` (optional) declares intermediate fit symbols that are added to the
    larch parameter group *before* the path parameters so any `constraints[].expr`
    can reference them. For example: `defs=[{"name":"alpha","value":0.0,"vary":true}]`
    plus `constraints=[{"name":"deltar","expr":"alpha"}]` models a uniform bond
    expansion driven by a single free `alpha`. Each def name must not duplicate
    a canonical parameter name.

    The report returns selected k/R bounds and each
    path's effective coordination number (fitted amplitude × FEFF degeneracy) and
    any highly-correlated parameter pairs.

ParamConstraint.description:
Optional per-parameter fit constraint (F4).

Lets an advanced user fix a parameter (``vary=False``), tighten its bounds
(``min``/``max``), override its starting/fixed ``value``, or link it to
another via a larch ``expr`` string (e.g. ``"dr_1"`` to tie one shell's ΔR
to another). ``name`` is the fit-parameter name: for a first-shell fit that
is ``amp``/``e0``/``sigma2``/``deltar``; for a multishell fit it is
``s02``/``e0`` or a per-shell ``ss2_<i>``/``dr_<i>``. Any field left ``None``
keeps the tool's default for that parameter.
ParamConstraint.title: ParamConstraint

ParamDef.description:
User-declared intermediate fit symbol (C1).

Adds a named parameter to the larch fit group *before* path parameters so
that any ``constraints[].expr`` or other ``ParamDef.expr`` can reference it.
Typical use: ``name="alpha", value=0.0, vary=True`` plus a constraint
``expr="alpha * reff"`` on a shell's ΔR to model correlated bond expansion.

``name`` must not duplicate a canonical fit-parameter name.  ``expr`` may
reference other ``ParamDef`` names defined in the same ``defs`` list.
ParamDef.title: ParamDef

tools.name: robust_first_shell_fit
tools.description:
`absorber` selects a chemical element in the CIF. Fits infer it only from a
unique measured-edge match; otherwise specify it explicitly. `edge` is the
measured edge family (K, L1, L2, L3; L means L3). Inconsistent spectra/CIFs fail.

This does the standard first-shell fit at the default k/R window AND re-runs it
across a small sweep of k-range and R-range settings to measure how much the
fitted parameters move (a sensitivity analysis), then runs the fit-quality

careful/robust/publication-quality fit or asks how trustworthy a fit is. Set
